The British No 1 was broken in all seven of her service games in a chastening 6-1 6-0 defeat inside 58 minutes on Louis Armstrong Stadium. Boulter traded breaks with Muchova at the start of the first set only for the 2026 Wimbledon finalist to pull clear and put on a clinic for her beleaguered opponent. Boulter double faulted eight times and produced 22 unforced errors in a nightmare, error-strewn performance that left her hopes of progressing in tatters. messages.text: Olympic gold medallist 'lucky to be alive' after car crash

metadata.summary: Olympic and world champion long jumper Tara Davis-Woodhall said she is ‘lucky to be alive’ after being involved in a head-on car collision while driving to training.
metadata.content: Tara Davis-Woodhall: Olympic long jump and world champion 'lucky to be alive' after being injured in car crash | Olympics News | Sky Sports Skip to content Tara Davis-Woodhall: Olympic long jump and world champion 'lucky to be alive' after being injured in car crash Tara Davis-Woodhall suffered concussion in a collision while heading to a training session last week; Davis-Woodhall, gold medallist at the Paris 2024 Olympics and last year's World Championships, was scheduled to appear at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship from September 11-13 Thursday 3 September 2026 06:44, UK Image: Tara Davis-Woodhall was injured in a car crash last week Olympic and world champion long jumper Tara Davis-Woodhall said she is ‘lucky to be alive’ after being involved in a head-on car collision while driving to training. American Davis-Woodhall, who won gold at the Paris 2024 Olympics and last year's World Championships in Tokyo, suffered 'no life-threatening' injuries but was concussed by the crash last week. The 27-year-old posted video of her crash - taken from a dashcam in her car - on social media, with Davis-Woodhall unsure whether she will be able to compete in this month's inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest. "Last week I was involved in a head on collision on my way to practice," Davis-Woodhall posted on Instagram. "I walked away with a concussion and other injuries that have prevented me from training.
